intervals.label: Long Shutdown 3
intervals.locator: home.cern/science/long-shutdown-3, item of 5 August 2026 "The LHC is being warmed up from near absolute zero to room temperature"
intervals.note: FASER detects particles produced in LHC collisions, so it is idle while the LHC is shut down; this is an inference, since no FASER-specific statement about this shutdown was found. Status is shutdown, not upgrade. The collaboration's home page (checked 2026-10-25) does not mention LS3 or an upgrade. No source consulted says that upgrade work on FASER is under way in LS3. FASER's collaboration plans an upgraded neutrino detector: 'The current plan is to implement the upgrade of the FASER detector by the start of the LHC Run 4.' (FASER Collaboration, arXiv:2503.19775, March 2025). That is a plan, not a report of work in progress. Start and end are the LHC-wide Long Shutdown 3 dates. CERN's 5 August 2026 item says 'The cryogenics team has been running the warm-up sequence since LS3 began on 29 June 2026' and that the stored helium is kept 'ready to be used again once the accelerator resumes operation in mid-2030'; CERN's 29 June 2026 article says 'The HiLumi LHC, scheduled to begin operation in 2030'. The end is a schedule value, not a reported event.
intervals.quote: Following its final physics run, the accelerator has been switched off to begin CERN’s Long Shutdown 3 (LS3) ... The HiLumi LHC, scheduled to begin operation in 2030

FASER cannot record anything while its only beam source (the LHC) is off for LS3, so its data-taking interval ends at the start of Long Shutdown 3 and its status is shutdown.

physics_goals.quote: Such particles may be produced in large numbers along the beam collision axis, travel for hundreds of meters without interacting, and then decay to standard model particles.
physics_goals.value: Search for light, extremely weakly-interacting particles (e.g. dark photons, ALPs, heavy neutral leptons) produced along the beam collision axis that would decay far from the interaction point

physics_goals.quote: FASER also has a subdetector called FASERν, which is specifically designed to detect neutrinos. No neutrino produced at a particle collider has ever been detected, despite colliders producing them in huge numbers and at high energies.
physics_goals.value: Detect and study high-energy neutrinos produced in LHC collisions via the FASERv subdetector, a first for a particle collider experiment

summary.plain: FASER is a small experiment placed in an unused tunnel 480 metres from CERN's ATLAS detector, watching for rare, long-lived particles and neutrinos that fly straight down the LHC's beamline.
summary.technical: Forward, long-lived-particle search experiment sited in the TI12 tunnel, 480 m downstream of ATLAS interaction point 1 along the beam collision axis; includes the FASERv emulsion/tungsten neutrino subdetector. Proposed September 2018, approved March 2019, installed during LS2 (2019-2021), data-taking July 2022 - June 2026 (LHC Run 3); off since CERN's Long Shutdown 3 began.

unique_capabilities.quote: FASER will complement the LHC's existing physics program, extending its discovery potential to a host of new, light particles
unique_capabilities.value: Located in an unused service tunnel directly along the beam collision axis, 480 m from ATLAS, exploiting a gap in the LHC's main-detector coverage to catch forward, long-lived and weakly-interacting particles
